clue.text: Undercover agent caught napping?

blocks.note: first meaning: a spy planted long before being activated
second meaning: someone found asleep

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second meaning: a spy who is literally asleep on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is both a dormant spy embedded in enemy territory and simply a person who is asleep.

clue.text: Comedian on the rise?

blocks.note: first meaning: a comic who performs solo to an audience
second meaning: getting to one's feet, rising upright

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rise' suggests a comic whose career is taking off; read literally it is getting to one's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up is a solo comic, and to stand up is to rise from sitting.

clue.text: One user or another is incorrect

indicators.note: another means a different version, so the letters are made into a different word

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A help desk insists that one customer or the other has got things wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Erroneous means containing errors, so wrong or incorrect.

clue.text: Initially pony's tail gets twisted into braid

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word
something twisted is bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first letter of pony's
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pony's tail is twisted into a braid for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A plait is a length of hair woven from three strands, the same thing as a braid.

clue.text: Continue to be embarrassed about having rest

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to remain is to continue being
red in the face from embarrassment

explanation.surface: Someone stays blushing about having needed a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' looks like sleep, but it is the noun meaning what is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is the part left over, the rest of something.

clue.text: Union has day to join

blocks.note: WED is the short form of Wednesday
to lock things is to fasten or join them together

explanation.surface: A trade union announces a day for new members to sign up.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedlock is the state of marriage, the union of two people.

clue.text: Grown out of evil

indicators.note: made out of means formed from these letters in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Something has developed from wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrong as a noun means immoral behaviour, so it is a synonym for evil.

clue.text: Tear apart underworld associate

blocks.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the underworld itself
an associate of a group is a member

explanation.surface: A gangland enforcer is ordered to rip apart a mob associate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld' suggests organised crime, which fits the violent surface; it is the classical realm of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismember is to cut or tear a body limb from limb, so to tear it apart.

clue.text: O to be Popeye's girl!

blocks.note: taken as written
to live is to exist, to be

explanation.surface: A wistful cry of longing to be the cartoon sailor's sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O' looks like the exclamation in 'O to be in England'; it is simply the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive Oyl is the girlfriend of the cartoon sailor Popeye.

clue.text: Desired, say, to be massaged

indicators.note: say tells you the word is spoken, so its sound is what counts

blocks.note: needed means wanted or desired

explanation.surface: A tired person longs to have a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading is pressing and working with the hands, so a kneaded muscle has been massaged.

clue.text: Big vessel from way back docked to take on volunteers

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the word loses its final letter
going back means the word is read from right to left
taking something on means adding it, so one piece is followed by another

blocks.note: a road is a way
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A large ship returns from a long journey, moors and takes on volunteer crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big vessel' suggests a ship, but it is the body's largest blood vessel. ROAD loses its D, then turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery leaving the heart, the largest blood vessel in the body.

clue.text: Illicit booze distilled by night light

blocks.note: first meaning: illegally distilled spirits
second meaning: light shed by the moon at night

explanation.surface: Bootleggers make their spirits secretly, working only by lamplight after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine is slang for illegally made liquor and also literally the light of the moon.

clue.text: University teacher, old and skinny, good to start, becomes a layabout

indicators.note: the start of the word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
O is a standard abbreviation for old
skinny means thin
the first letter of good

explanation.surface: An elderly, scrawny academic who started out well ends up idling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good to start' reads as the G coming first, but it means only the opening letter of good, which goes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A do-nothing is an idle person who avoids work, which is exactly what a layabout is.

clue.text: Make improvement with online repair?

blocks.note: E as in e-mail stands for electronic, so online
to mend is to repair

explanation.surface: Fixing something with a quick internet repair to make it better.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct or improve a text, so it means making an improvement.

clue.text: Arrogant dropout's hanging round university

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the letters before it are rearranged
hanging round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: the word splits as drop + out; only the first half is fodder, the second half being the signal to rearrange
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A haughty student who quit still loiters around the campus.
explanation.walkthrough: The word dropout splits in two: DROP is the fodder and out tells you to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud can mean having too high an opinion of oneself, which is arrogance.

clue.text: Get rid of smell by flapping side door with energy

indicators.note: something flapping moves loosely back and forth, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Airing a stuffy room by vigorously swinging the side door open and shut.
explanation.definitionFit: To deodorise is to remove or mask an unpleasant odour.

clue.text: Objective of in-pub entertainment?

blocks.note: surface reading: the purpose or aim of having fun in a pub
setter's reading: objective as a target, the thing players aim at in a classic pub game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' sounds abstract, a goal or purpose; read literally it is the physical target thrown at in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Darts is a traditional British pub game, and the board is what every throw aims for.

clue.text: Storyteller has traitor keeping company with knight on last ride to ancient city

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece is enclosed
last points to the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: a rat is a betrayer
Co is the abbreviation for company
N is knight in chess notation
the final letter of ride
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A tale of a traitor riding with a knight to an ancient city, told by a bard.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a person skilled at telling anecdotes and stories.

clue.text: Wealth of disease in a hedge

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second

blocks.note: a hedge acts as a fence, with the article taken as written
flu is a common disease

explanation.surface: A blight spreading through a hedgerow.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluence is the state of having plenty of money, i.e. wealth.

clue.text: See inside Punjabi shop rich go to

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and most of the third

explanation.surface: Look inside a wealthy Punjabi store and you will want to go there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an instruction to look; it is a bishop's see.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is the diocese or office of a bishop, which is also called a bishopric.

clue.text: Second-rate prophet gets first lady to have faith

blocks.note: B grade is second-rate
Eli is the priest and prophet who raised Samuel in the Bible
Eve was the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A mediocre preacher persuades the President's wife to become a believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' suggests a President's wife; it is the Bible's first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To believe is to have faith or trust in something.

clue.text: Works hard to lose gravity and floats

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away from the word

blocks.note: to graft is British slang for working hard
G is the symbol for gravity

explanation.surface: Someone toils to escape gravity and drift weightlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the G from GRAFTS. 'Graft' meaning hard work is everyday British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Rafts are flat floating platforms, so they are floats used on water.

clue.text: Please express opinion about outfits

indicators.note: out means out of order, so the letters after it are rearranged
about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: to say is to express an opinion
the word splits as out + fits; only the second half is fodder, the first half being the signal to rearrange

explanation.surface: A shopper asks a friend for their honest view on some clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The word outfits splits in two: out tells you to rearrange FITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to satisfy them, to give them what they want.

clue.text: Fire takes time to penetrate building blocks

indicators.note: penetrating something means getting inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Lego is the toy brick system
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A blaze slowly burns through a child's pile of toy bricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like flames, but it is the verb meaning to dismiss from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone go is a euphemism for dismissing them from employment, i.e. firing them.

clue.text: Raise glass when in shot

indicators.note: in puts the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: a tot is a small shot of spirits
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Lifting your glass while appearing in a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast someone is to raise a glass and drink in their honour.

clue.text: Criticise for duff Latin translation

indicators.note: a translation turns words into a different form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher marks down a pupil's poor attempt at rendering Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duff' is British slang for bad or useless, which fits the surface; here it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To find fault is an idiom meaning to complain about or criticise something.

clue.text: Fine artist to measure up for picture mount

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top

blocks.note: F is the pencil grade for fine
RA is a Royal Academician
an em is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A good artist sizing up a mount for a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame is the border in which a picture is set or mounted.

clue.text: Failed to remember detailed forfeit

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, the word loses its tail, its last letter

blocks.note: forgot means failed to remember

explanation.surface: A forgotten detailed form leads to a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like thorough, but split it as de-tailed: cut off the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo is to give up or do without, which is what forfeiting something means.

clue.text: Get rid of hesitation about idea: act!

indicators.note: about can mean moved around, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: er is the sound of someone hesitating
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Stop dithering over the plan and act to wipe the problem out!
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to destroy completely, so to get rid of something entirely.

clue.text: Queen breaks off in tears

blocks.note: R is for Regina, Latin for queen
to break off is to end

explanation.surface: The monarch abruptly stops speaking, overcome and crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' suggests weeping, but it is the verb rhyming with bears: rips.
explanation.definitionFit: Rends means rips or pulls apart violently, as tears does when pronounced to rhyme with bears.

clue.text: SMS lost beginning about me being radical

indicators.note: losing its beginning means the word drops its first letter

blocks.note: an SMS is a text message
re means about, concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lost text message about me is taken as evidence of my radical views.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme and radical both describe views far from the moderate centre.

clue.text: Castle has strange eyrie that is cut out for birds to nest in

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a nesting place, standing for a noun

indicators.note: something cut out is removed from the word it sat in
strange means odd or out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the castle in chess is also called the rook
taken as written
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A castle tower contains an odd eagle's nest, purpose-built for nesting birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I and E from EYRIE, then rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookery is a colony of rooks' nests in treetops, a place where birds breed.
